title: Source-edit skill-lock live hole (RESOLVED): catch-all did not fire on Edit/Write
desc: BUG reproduced 2026-06-07 and RESOLVED. The source-edit catch-all skill-lock did NOT block an unregistered source file edited via the built-in Edit/Write tool -- proven by an Opus root Write of an unregistered probe.cs SUCCEEDING (expected RC 2). Root cause was NOT the matcher (the hook runs for all tools) but a fail-OPEN crash. Kept as the canonical repro + fix record.
steps: REPRO: as an Opus root session, Write a new unregistered source file (e.g. a probe .cs). EXPECTED RC 2 catch-all block. ACTUAL (the bug): the Write succeeded -- the source-edit skill-lock was bypassed for the Edit/Write tool path. Confirmed live 2026-06-07.
NOT the matcher: settings.json PreToolUse runs wkharness.ps1 with NO matcher so it fires for Edit/Write too. The bypass was INSIDE the load chain.

ROOT CAUSE: wkharness.ps1 called Initialize-WkGeminiSession but never dot-sourced wkharness-gemini.ps1 -> every tool call threw -> the top-level catch printed an unexpected-error line and exited 0 (fail-OPEN) -> the catch-all and skill-lock NEVER ran. A single missing dot-source silently disabled ALL guards. Diagnosed by feeding a probe Write JSON to wkharness.ps1 and seeing the gemini error with no deny.
FIX: added the wkharness-gemini.ps1 dot-source before the call. VERIFIED: a real Edit of an unregistered .cs then returned RC 2 no-skill-rule, blocking even my own edit.

LESSON: a fail-open crash in a guard chain is invisible -- it does not block, it just stops protecting. Verify guards by a REAL edit that SHOULD be blocked, not by assuming silence means safe. Cross-ref harness-robustness-user-dist-appbot-absent, harness-source-edit-requires-skill-lock, harness-edit-write-skill-bypass.
